agree.reason: A quick reader gets concrete, credible signals (sole 3 a.m. shift, nine early mastitis cases worth about $8,000, a job kept open part-time) that make Tomás stand out among 150 applicants, though nothing speaks directly to whether he can handle coursework.

honest.reason: "In three years he has missed two shifts" drops the brief's qualifier "not counting those 5 weeks," so the attendance claim is stronger than the facts allow, and details like "signed up on his own" and the parlor being "left ready" are made up.

works_the_facts.reason: The letter uses the $8,000 vet estimate and the nine cases well, but it leaves the attendance record as a bare count when a rate (two missed out of roughly 750 solo shifts) would carry more weight.

right_comparison.reason: There's an implied comparison ("I don't hand a shift like that to many people") but nothing that places Tomás against a typical worker or applicant beyond that one remark.

qualification.reason: A reference letter of this kind needs no conditional hedge; its commitments (weekend job, phone call) are stated plainly.

objections.reason: The written-English worry is met head-on with the night class, but the 5-week absence is hidden instead of turned into a strength (he arranged cover and came back on the day he promised), which leaves the attendance claim open to challenge if the absence comes up.

fit.reason: It's a one-page letter from the farm manager in a plain, suitable register, with contact details and a signature, though it has no date.
